content:
maria: Quick heads-up — profiler found a regression after yesterday's autotune change. p95 tail for long sequences jumped.
maria: Summary: A100, model redwood-3b, seqlen bin 768-1024, p95 went from ~82ms to ~142ms between deployes at 09:12 and 09:40 UTC.
li: :eyes: Do we have traces? Is it kernel selection or KV hit-rate drop?
devon: I pulled flame graphs. Looks like more time in kernel dispatch and also an extra memcpy path when the driver falls back to generic matmul.
sasha: attaching profiler snippets (copied):

```
CPU: driver dispatch 12ms -> 34ms
GPU kernel launch overhead + queueing 18ms -> 46ms
KV cache lookup p99 unchanged ~0.6ms
KV hit-rate down 0.98 -> 0.93 for seq-prefixes >512
```

maria: So two signals: wrong kernel picks for some seqlen/arch combos + subtle KV key-mismatch causing extra cache misses.
li: That key mismatch rings a bell — we recently changed key salting to include driver_id to avoid cross-driver clobbering. Could be we didn't include model variant tag.
devon: Right. Current key format: `{model_name}:{driver_id}:{prefix_hash}`. New autotune introduces seqlen binning on key: some code paths still compute seqlen_bin differently (floor vs bucket), causing inconsistent keys across runtime upgrades.
sasha: Repro snippet I used to detect missing salt:

```python
def make_key(model, driver, prefix, seqlen):
    seqbin = (seqlen // 256) * 256  # old behavior
    return f"{model}:{driver}:{seqbin}:{hash(prefix) & 0xffffffff}"

# new code used math.ceil -> different seqbin for seqlen=768
```

maria: So inconsistent keying + a kernel routing change -> more cache misses and also non-optimal kernel selected when KV miss triggers a longer exec path.
li: Proposed short-term fix: roll back seqlen-binning code path to canonical floor-based binning until we have compatibility migration.
devon: Longer term: introduce a key version and a migration plan. Key format v2 should be explicit e.g. `v2:{model}:{model_hash}:{driver}:{seqbin_v2}:{prefix_hash}` so we can coexist and fallback.

sasha: Perf/regression test plan I suggest:
- microbench: kernel-selector unit tests across archs (A100, H100 emu) and seqlen boundaries (255/256, 511/512, 767/768, 1023/1024)
- kv-sanity: replay 24h production prefix sample to validate hit-rate delta
- e2e: canary traffic 1% with v2 keys and fallback logic for reads

maria: Also need autopopulate script to backfill the v2 cache entries for hot prefixes to avoid cold-start storm post-migration.
li: Backfill outline: sample top-1000 prefixes from metrics, compute v2 keys, prewarm via warmup RPCs to Dedicated pools overnight.
devon: Important: persistence format change — we store key metadata in RocksDB with TTLs. Must guarantee old keys don't get prematurely evicted during backfill window. Increase TTL for backfill cohort to 72h during migration.

atlas-bot: CI note: perf-tests/kernel-selector now failing 2/50 flakes — failing on seqlen=768 boundaries. Job: job-8472
ci-bot: job-8472 logs available: https://ci.internal/redwood/job-8472/console

sasha: Checklist for rollout:
1) revert seqbin change in runtime (hotfix) -> monitor p95 for 30m
2) cut v2 key schema RFC and land library that supports dual-read fallback
3) run backfill job targeting top prefixes
4) canary v2 read-only on 1% traffic for 6h, check p95 + kv hit-rate
5) promote to 10% for 12h, then full read/write

maria: Who can take 1) now? This looks like immediate mitigation.
li: I'm on it. Will open a rollback PR and include the original unit tests. ETA 20m.
devon: I'll own items 2/3 (key RFC + backfill). Will draft RFC today and start backfill job once pr is merged.
sasha: I'll own the perf test harness updates and add seqlen boundary cases. Also will pin test infra to run on A100 for the next 24h :thumbsup:
maria: Great. Please post PR links here and add the canary dashboard to the runbook. Thanks all :heart!
